title: How Are LLMs Mitigating Stereotyping Harms? Learning from Search Engine Studies
benchmark_measurement: Detection of stereotypes and harmful content related to various religious groups, evaluated through autocomplete-style, open-ended text generation prompts. The study measured refusal rates, toxicity, sentiment, and regard of the LLM responses.
findings: The 'religion' category obtained among the highest regard scores overall. However, refusal rates varied, with the category having one of the lowest refusal rates in aggregate, but specific groups like 'Jews' triggered high rates of refusal from models like Llama, Mistral, and Starling. Responses concerning Atheists, Mormons, and Muslims were characterized by lower sentiment, while those for Buddhists, Catholics, Protestants, and Christians scored high. No toxic responses were found for 'Jews', but the paper notes that stereotyping towards Muslims persists in LLMs, a contrast to moderation practices in search engines.
